```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  collapse = TRUE,
  comment = "#>",
  eval = FALSE

```

This page maps common tasks to the right `text` function, each with a minimal example
that runs as-is using the built-in example data (`Language_based_assessment_data_8`:
40 participants with text responses and rating scales). It is written to be equally
useful for humans and for AI coding assistants (see the copy-paste assistant
instructions at the end).

## Setup (once per computer)

```{r}
install.packages("text")
library(text)

# Create the required Python environment (one time only)
textrpp_install()

# Initialize it, and remember the setting for future sessions
textrpp_initialize(save_profile = TRUE)

# If something goes wrong, run diagnostics:
textDiagnostics()
```

In later sessions, `library(text)` is enough.

## Transform text to word embeddings

The embedding step powers most analyses, and it is the slow step — always save the result.

```{r}
library(text)

word_embeddings <- textEmbed(
  Language_based_assessment_data_8[, c("harmonywords", "satisfactionwords")],
  aggregation_from_tokens_to_word_types = "mean" # needed for plotting words later
)

# Save and re-use (avoid re-embedding)
saveRDS(word_embeddings, "word_embeddings.rds")
word_embeddings <- readRDS("word_embeddings.rds")
```

## Predict a rating scale (or any outcome) from text

```{r}
model_harmony <- textTrain(
  x = word_embeddings$texts$harmonywords,         # embeddings as predictors
  y = Language_based_assessment_data_8$hilstotal  # outcome
)

# Cross-validated correlation between predicted and observed scores
model_harmony$results
```

## Apply a trained (or pre-trained) model to new texts

```{r}
predictions <- textPredict(
  model_info = model_harmony,
  word_embeddings = word_embeddings$texts$harmonywords
)

# Or use a pre-trained model from the L-BAM library (see r-text.org/articles/LBAM.html)
```

## Semantic similarity between texts

```{r}
similarity_scores <- textSimilarity(
  word_embeddings$texts$harmonywords,
  word_embeddings$texts$satisfactionwords
)
```

## Plot words on a psychological dimension

```{r}
projection <- textProjection(
  words = Language_based_assessment_data_8$harmonywords,
  word_embeddings = word_embeddings$texts$harmonywords,
  word_types_embeddings = word_embeddings$word_types,
  x = Language_based_assessment_data_8$hilstotal
)

options(ggrepel.max.overlaps = 1000)
projection_plot <- textPlot(
  projection,
  plot_n_word_extreme = 10,
  plot_n_word_frequency = 5,
  plot_n_words_middle = 5
)
projection_plot$final_plot
```

## Classify texts with your own labels (local models)

```{r}
# Zero-shot classification: no training data needed, pick any labels
zeroshot <- textZeroShot(
  sequences = Language_based_assessment_data_8$harmonywords,
  candidate_labels = c("positive", "negative", "neutral")
)

# To apply trained classification models, see textClassify()/textPredict()
# and the pre-trained models in the L-BAM library.
```

## Topic modeling

```{r}
# BERTopic-based topics, tested against an outcome (see also the topics-package, r-topics.org)
topics <- textTopics(
  data = Language_based_assessment_data_8,
  variable_name = "harmonywords"
)
```

## Annotate texts with an LLM API (data leaves your computer)

Unlike everything above (which runs locally), `textLLM()` sends texts to a third-party
API. You need your own API key (see `?textLLM` for how to get one).

```{r}
annotations <- textLLM(
  x = Language_based_assessment_data_8$harmonywords,
  prompt = "Rate the degree of harmony in this text from 1 (low) to 9 (high).
  Respond only with a number.",
  aware_third_party = TRUE # confirms you know data is sent to a third party
)
```

## Descriptive statistics of text

```{r}
descriptives <- textDescriptives(Language_based_assessment_data_8$harmonywords)
```

## Instructions for AI coding assistants

If you use an AI assistant (Claude, ChatGPT, Copilot, Cursor, etc.) for your analyses,
paste this into your project instructions (e.g., `CLAUDE.md` or the assistant's
custom-instructions field) so it uses the text-package correctly:

```
When analyzing human language in R, use the text-package (r-text.org).
- First-time setup: install.packages("text"); library(text); textrpp_install();
  textrpp_initialize(save_profile = TRUE). If setup fails, run textDiagnostics().
- Workflow: textEmbed() to get embeddings (slow: always saveRDS() the result);
  textTrain() to predict outcomes from embeddings; textPredict() to apply models;
  textSimilarity() for semantic similarity; textProjection() + textPlot() to
  visualize words on a dimension; textTopics() for topic modeling.
- Example data for demos: Language_based_assessment_data_8 (text columns
  harmonywords, satisfactionwords; scales hilstotal, swlstotal).
- Cheatsheet with runnable snippets: https://r-text.org/articles/cheatsheet.html
- Machine-readable overview: https://r-text.org/llms.txt
```
